tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to orders and goods receipts and book them.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives as a UBL e-invoice, a PDF in AFAS Profit, or an email in Outlook.
steps: Open the invoice and find the purchase order and the goods receipt for Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo.
Compare supplier, quantity, price, VAT and the agreed terms.
Code the ledger account, VAT code and site, or accept what AFAS proposed.
Book the invoice and send it for payment approval, or park the difference.
Chase a missing receipt or order with the buyer or the warehouse.
drudgery: Retyping lines from a PDF that has no UBL.
Searching Outlook for an order number the invoice does not show.
Coding the same supplier to the same account again.
today.time_sinks: PDFs without UBL, partial deliveries, price differences, night-shift receipts that are not in AFAS yet, and agency invoices that must be tied to approved hours before the g-rekening split.

lenses.faster: Typing invoice lines and searching for the order disappear when a UBL invoice matches the order and the receipt on supplier, amount and reference. What stays is the exception, a price or quantity difference, a missing receipt or a new supplier, still several minutes each, plus a short look at the match log, so about a third of today's time remains.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the invoice reaches AFAS. The match and the booking of a clean one-to-one run without the bookkeeper. The gate is a difference, a missing receipt, a new supplier, or a changed IBAN.
lenses.ambitious: A new weekly settlement for the controller and the three staffing agencies splits each agency invoice into the wage-tax and VAT part for the g-rekening and the remainder, and sends only hour differences back. Demand would grow in the peak, when flex headcount moves from 150 to 300, because that check is the first work dropped when the team is behind.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing PDF lines and hunting for order numbers in mail. The work they want more of is the price, waiting-time and damage differences that change what Noordhaven pays.
lenses.options: Holding an invoice for a credit note, short-paying it, or booking the gap to a price-difference account changes the creditor balance and whether a small supplier is paid inside the legal 30 days. Those are different decisions.
lenses.altitude: The week is the exception queue and supplier records, and the bookkeeper can set a match tolerance and block a supplier whose KvK number or IBAN does not agree, inside limits the controller sets. The job becomes more expert, centred on commercial differences and hirer's liability.
reach: The accountant's correction of wrongly coded purchase invoices during the close, after the bookkeeper learns the transport VAT treatments and the cost centers of the three sites.

tasks.human_edge: The person judges waiting-time, fuel and damage charges that a price match cannot price, and spots a supplier whose IBAN or Chamber of Commerce record looks wrong. With the controller, the person also decides when an agency's payment-behaviour statement is too old to rely on for hirer's liability.
tasks.pattern_why: Supplier, order, amount, quantity and VAT can be written as match rules, and AFAS already books a one-to-one hit. A model is not required for that match; scan-and-recognise fills a PDF and leaves the gaps on the same exception list.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice lands in AFAS as UBL or as a scanned PDF.
steps: AFAS matches UBL, or recognised lines, to the order and the goods receipt on supplier, amount and reference.
A one-to-one match inside the tolerance is booked and queued for payment approval.
A PDF without UBL is recognised and the supplier is taken from KvK number, VAT number and IBAN, with empty fields flagged.
Price, quantity, missing-receipt, new-supplier and agency-hour differences go to one exception list.
The bookkeeper accepts, splits, or returns each exception, and splits an agency invoice onto the g-rekening.
in_practice.human_gate: Every exception and every first-time supplier. Clean one-to-one matches post without retyping. Payment approval stays with the authorised approver, and an agency invoice with an hour difference or a missing g-rekening split stays with the bookkeeper.
data_needed: Purchase orders and goods receipts by site
Supplier master with KvK, VAT number and IBAN
Ledger accounts, VAT codes and site cost centers
Agency hour approvals, g-rekening share and payment-behaviour statement
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS booking and approval trail: source document, match rule, proposed and accepted codes, and the person who released each exception.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level, and a one-to-one match with an order or a receipt is booked and approved for payment. The partner report gives no match rate.
A PDF without UBL is scanned into an e-invoice. The supplier is found from KvK number, VAT number and IBAN, and the gaps are filled by hand.
A booking proposal is not the same as touchless processing. Own ledger accounts, VAT codes, exceptions per administration, and PDFs keep a person in the flow.
A hirer can be liable for a staffing agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT, and limits that by record-keeping, a payment-behaviour statement, and paying that part into the agency's g-rekening.

risks: A wrong VAT code or ledger account on a clean match repeats on later invoices from that supplier and shows up as a close or audit adjustment.
A wide tolerance hides a real price increase.
Posting an agency invoice without the g-rekening split leaves Noordhaven exposed for the agency's wage tax and VAT.
Approval that still happens in Outlook can push a small supplier past the legal 30-day maximum and can miss a short intra-EU reporting window once that regime starts.
research_questions: What share of invoices arrives as UBL, and what share as PDF, for carriers, warehouse suppliers and the three agencies?
What does AFAS match on the first pass today, and which exceptions dominate: price, quantity, missing receipt, VAT or new supplier?
Is the g-rekening percentage and a recent payment-behaviour statement on file per agency, and can approved flex hours be read from the agency portal?
Do approvers work in AFAS or by email, and what is the median time from receipt to payment approval? A multi-day mail round would cap the gain and put the 30-day rule at risk.

tasks.short: Enter debits and credits in AFAS and total the accounts.

today.trigger: A batch of coded invoices, a bank file, or a request for a correction journal is ready to post.
steps: Open the AFAS journal or the Excel workbook kept beside it.
Enter the debit and credit with ledger account, VAT code, cost center and site.
Total the batch and check that debits equal credits.
When Excel and AFAS differ, find the line that caused it.
Post the journal or leave it for the accountant.
drudgery: Adding columns to prove a total the ledger already has.
Copying AFAS totals into a workbook for someone else.
Retyping the same accrual each month.
today.time_sinks: Journals that fail on the VAT line, waiting a night for the Power BI extract to show whether the posting landed, and cost centers for three sites.

lenses.faster: Re-keying and re-adding in Excel disappear for any entry AFAS already holds as a balanced journal. A manual journal still takes a few minutes to check the description, the VAT line and the source, and about a third of today's time remains on that queue.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a matched document is ready or a recurring journal date arrives. AFAS posts the balanced entry and its totals without the bookkeeper. The gate is a manual journal, a suspense account, or a batch total that does not match the source.
lenses.ambitious: A new same-day note to the two FP&A analysts shows what was posted per site, so the forecast does not wait for the nightly Power BI refresh. Demand would grow in close week, when the analysts now rebuild that gap by hand and would ask for the note on every close day if it were cheap.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss cross-adding a workbook to prove that AFAS can add. The work they want more of is a correction journal that changes what a site's costs look like.
lenses.options: Posting a correction to another site, accruing it, or leaving it on suspense changes the month's result and which site manager sees the cost. The draft they accept is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week is a short queue of manual journals and a look at suspense, and the bookkeeper can release recurring journals and routine reclasses up to a limit the controller sets. The job becomes more expert on whether the entry is fair, and less of it is data entry.
reach: The accountant's standard recurring accruals for rent, energy and prepayments, after the bookkeeper learns the close calendar and the materiality limit the controller uses. The accountant keeps unusual items.

tasks.human_edge: The person sees a journal that balances and is still wrong, such as Venlo's costs sitting on Rotterdam, or a credit on a VAT code that flatters the result. The ledger can balance the lines; the person knows the story.
tasks.pattern_why: Debits, credits, VAT and batch totals are rules the ledger already enforces. A model adds nothing to a total that AFAS can compute, and the free-typed journals stay on an exception queue with a person.

in_practice.trigger: A matched source document is ready to post, or the date of a recurring journal arrives.
steps: AFAS posts the balanced journal from the matched invoice, the bank line, or a stored recurring entry.
The ledger calculates the total and the VAT.
An out-of-balance line, a suspense account, or a manual journal is queued.
The bookkeeper checks the manual queue against the source and posts it or returns it.
Site totals for the day are available in AFAS for FP&A without a second workbook.
in_practice.human_gate: Every manual journal, every posting to suspense, and any batch whose total does not match the source document.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT codes
The controller's limit for a routine reclass
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS journal audit: user, time, source document, and the reason on any manual or suspense line.

evidence.claim: A one-to-one invoice match in AFAS is booked as a ledger entry and approved for payment, so the debit and credit are created by that posting.
Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration are why a booking proposal still needs a person, and measured touchless shares disappoint.
Re-adding, in a spreadsheet, figures the ledger already totals is ordinary arithmetic on structured data and does not need a model.

risks: A recurring journal keeps posting after the contract or the amount has changed.
Suspense becomes a parking place and returns at the close as an audit adjustment.
A workbook kept beside AFAS drifts from the ledger and from the nightly Power BI extract, and two totals circulate.
research_questions: What share of journal lines is posted by an invoice or bank match, by a recurring template, or by a free-typed entry?
Which Excel workbooks still total figures AFAS already stores, and who treats those workbooks as the figure they use?
How often does a journal fail the balance or the VAT check, and what are the usual causes?
Do the FP&A analysts read AFAS during the day, or only the nightly Power BI extract? If they already read AFAS, the new note has little value.

tasks.short: Code costs to the ledger, the VAT code and the site.

today.trigger: An invoice or a cost batch is not yet coded, or someone asks for a summary by supplier, account or site.
steps: Read the invoice text and the attachments.
Look up the supplier's usual ledger account, VAT code and site.
Split a multi-site or mixed invoice across cost centers.
Record the lines in AFAS.
Build a summary in Excel when the accountant or FP&A asks for one.
drudgery: Scrolling the chart of accounts for a code used last week.
Re-coding a supplier that always posts to one account.
Rebuilding the same summary in Excel.
today.time_sinks: Invoices that mix transport, fuel and waiting time, an unclear site, domestic VAT versus reverse charge, and new suppliers with no history.

lenses.faster: Searching the chart of accounts disappears when the supplier has one usual code, and a proposal fills the lines that history cannot close. Accepting a good proposal takes under a minute; splitting a mixed invoice still takes several minutes, so about half of today's time remains.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when capture finishes and supplier history does not give one code. One model call proposes the ledger account, VAT code and site. Nothing posts until the bookkeeper accepts or edits it.
lenses.ambitious: The VAT treatment, domestic, intra-EU or reverse charge, is decided when a supplier or its VAT number is new, including the small carriers that are coded from habit today. Demand grows if that check is cheap, because the bookkeeper now stops only for a foreign or unusually large invoice.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting the chart of accounts for a familiar supplier. The work they want more of is the mixed invoice, where the split between sites and between freight and surcharge changes the result.
lenses.options: Coding a mixed invoice all to Rotterdam, splitting it from the delivery notes, or parking it on suspense changes the site result and the VAT box. The accepted draft is the figure the controller sees at the close.
lenses.altitude: The week is a review of proposals and a fix to supplier defaults that keep producing the wrong code. The bookkeeper can set a supplier's default account and VAT code so the next invoice does not ask, inside the chart the accountant owns. The job becomes more expert on VAT and on the site split.
reach: The accountant's first pass on VAT-code corrections before the return, after the bookkeeper learns when transport is domestic, intra-EU or reverse-charged, and which cases to hand back. The accountant keeps the return.

tasks.human_edge: The person chooses the account when a cost could fairly sit in two places, such as forklift repair versus forklift hire, or detention versus the freight rate. History suggests the usual code; the person knows what the warehouse bought.
tasks.pattern_why: A supplier with one stable code is a rule and needs no model. The work that remains is invoice text that does not pick a single account, VAT code or site, and one model call turns that text into a proposal inside a fixed accept-or-edit step. The steps do not change from invoice to invoice, so an agent is the wrong pattern.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice is captured and supplier history does not give a single ledger account and VAT code.
steps: A stored rule fills account, VAT code and site when that supplier's history is one code.
Where history is split or the PDF is unclear, one model call proposes the coding and shows the line text it used.
The proposal sits next to the invoice for the bookkeeper to accept or edit.
Accepted lines post, and an edit updates the supplier default only when the bookkeeper says it should.
Summaries by supplier, account and site come from AFAS.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper accepts or changes every proposal the history rule did not close. A new supplier and a new ledger account are always a human accept.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT table
Written coding notes on SharePoint, if they exist
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS, with the proposed code, the accepted code, the line text used, and the person who changed it.

evidence.claim: After scan-and-recognise, gaps on a PDF invoice are filled by hand. Supplier identity comes from KvK number, VAT number and IBAN.
In a NetSuite case, Escalante Golf cut handling from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice. Coding was suggested from vendor history for a person to review and confirm.
Own ledger accounts and VAT codes are a main reason a booking proposal does not become touchless processing.
AP decisions should be logged with the data that produced them, and people should remain on the exceptions.

risks: A fluent proposal names the wrong site or the wrong VAT treatment, and a busy reviewer accepts it.
Supplier history locks in last year's mistake and applies it to every new invoice.
Invoice text can contain personal names. The proposal step should keep that text in AFAS and should not copy it into a general prompt log.
research_questions: For what share of suppliers are the ledger account and VAT code unchanged over the last twelve months? A high share means a history rule is enough and a model step is unnecessary.
How many VAT-code corrections does the accountant make when preparing the return?
Are coding rules written on SharePoint, or only remembered by the team?
Does AFAS scan already propose a ledger account, and how often is that proposal posted unchanged?

tasks.short: Bring journal and bank totals into the general ledger.

today.trigger: A source journal is finished, or a Rabobank file, payroll file or agency file is ready to move.
steps: Export or open the source journal or the incoming file.
Map the columns onto the ledger layout or an Excel processing sheet.
Import or copy the batch into AFAS.
Check the imported total against the source.
Fix rejected rows by hand.
drudgery: Copying a total from one AFAS screen onto another.
Rebuilding the same Excel bridge every period.
Re-importing a file because a column moved.
today.time_sinks: Agency files whose supplier number does not match AFAS, a bank file for the wrong account, and a payroll journal that arrives after the close has started.

lenses.faster: The second copying of a journal into the ledger or onto a processing sheet disappears where AFAS already posted the entry. A control-total check is a few minutes per batch, and a failed row takes about as long as today, so about a third of the time remains.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a subledger entry is posted or a bank, payroll or agency file arrives. The import and the posting run on a stored mapping. The gate is a rejected row, a new file layout, or a total that does not tie to the source.
lenses.ambitious: A new morning list for the controller, used in close week, shows which journals have not reached the ledger: payroll, the three agency files and Rabobank. Demand would grow if the list were cheap, because a missing file is now found late and the controller would use it after every payroll run and every close.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying totals between screens. The work they want more of is a file that loaded and is still the wrong week, the wrong account or a duplicate.
lenses.options: Posting a late agency or bank file in the open period or in the next one changes the close. Two mappings of the same file can also hit different suppliers, so the mapping draft changes the creditors.
lenses.altitude: The transfer afternoon leaves the week. The bookkeeper spends that time on mappings that broke and on telling the controller which files are in, and can release a file that ties and hold one that does not. The job becomes more expert on cut-off and on the interfaces.
reach: The accountant's check that subledgers tie to the general ledger at the start of the close, after the bookkeeper learns the control totals and the cut-off rules. The accountant keeps the analytical review.

tasks.human_edge: The person notices a file that imported without error and is still last week's statement, the wrong legal entity, or a second copy of the same bank file. A balanced import can be the wrong import, and that call stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Which journal, which account and which period are mapping rules, and AFAS already posts a matched invoice without a second transfer. Failed rows are predictable exceptions, so an agent or a model is not required to move the batch.

in_practice.trigger: A subledger batch is posted, or a Rabobank CAMT.053 file, payroll file or agency file arrives.
steps: AFAS carries subledger totals into the general ledger as part of the original entry.
Bank, payroll and agency files import on a stored mapping.
Rows that fail the mapping or the control total land on one list.
The bookkeeper corrects the mapping or the source reference and releases those rows.
A batch that ties is released without retyping.
in_practice.human_gate: A failed row, a file layout the mapping has not seen, and any total that does not tie to the source. Cut-off into a closed period stays with the controller.
data_needed: Control totals from each source file
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS import log: file name, row counts, source total, posted total, and the person who released the exceptions.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 bank lines with rules on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then oldest-first sums. Misses go to a person. Exact amounts apply unless a tolerance is set.
A matched purchase invoice is booked in AFAS, so those lines do not need a separate journal transfer into the ledger.
Copying the same totals onto a data-processing sheet, once the ledger is the record, is spreadsheet arithmetic on data the system already holds.

risks: A mapping that is slightly wrong can post a whole file to the wrong supplier or the wrong period and still agree on the total.
Importing the same CAMT file twice can double a balance if the duplicate check fails.
An agency portal changes its file layout without notice and the next import fails on the morning it is needed.
research_questions: Which sources still move by Excel or by file import: Rabobank, payroll, the three agency portals, and any others?
How often do those imports fail, and is the cause the layout, the supplier number, a duplicate, or the total?
Is Noordhaven one AFAS administration with site cost centers, or more than one administration? More than one changes the mapping work.
Which control total does the accountant still tie by hand at the close, and how long does that take? If it is already a one-screen check, most of this task has already gone.

tasks.short: Clear the bank against open items and report what is left.

today.trigger: The Rabobank statement is in, or it is time for the open-item review.
steps: Import the bank statement into AFAS.
Match lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount.
Clear the matches and leave the rest open.
Investigate a partial payment, a lump sum, a missing reference or a timing difference.
Write the discrepancy to the accountant, the credit and collections officer, or the supplier.
drudgery: Ticking payments that match to the cent.
Copying the unmatched list into Excel for the weekly review.
Re-reading a statement that was already imported.
today.time_sinks: Customers who pay several invoices in one amount, missing references, payments from an unknown IBAN, and agency payments that still need a g-rekening check.

lenses.faster: Ticking the exact matches disappears once AFAS clears them on reference, IBAN, invoice number or amount. Each line that stays still takes several minutes to identify and to write up, and that tail is most of the remaining time, a bit under half of today.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the Rabobank statement is imported. AFAS clears lines the rules can explain. The gate is every line left open, and any match that uses a tolerance above the limit the controller allows.
lenses.ambitious: A new same-day short-pay note to the credit and collections officer names the customer, the invoices the money covered, and the amount still open. Demand would grow if the note were cheap, because small short-pays are skipped today and only the large ones are chased.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss ticking lines that agree to the cent. The work they want more of is the break that explains something real: a customer who deducted a claim, or money on the wrong account.
lenses.options: Allocating a lump-sum receipt oldest-first, largest-first, or by the customer's remittance changes which invoices stay open and which customer the credit officer calls. The allocation is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week is the unmatched queue and a short note to the credit officer or the controller. The bookkeeper can clear inside the tolerance and allocate a lump sum when the remittance supports one reading. The job becomes more expert on how customers pay.
reach: The credit and collections officer's preparation of the weekly open-item list, after the bookkeeper learns which short-pays are disputes and what the DSO target is. The officer keeps the customer call and any payment plan.

tasks.human_edge: The person reads a remittance that contradicts the amount, recognises a customer who always deducts damage, and treats an unknown IBAN as a stop. The rule sees two numbers; the person knows the relationship and the fraud signal.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already matches the bank on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount, and the match log states which rule failed. That is enough to report the discrepancy. A model is only a later option if the note must be prose drawn from an email, and the steps of the reconciliation itself stay rules.

in_practice.trigger: A Rabobank CAMT.053 file is imported, or the period-end open-item run starts.
steps: AFAS matches on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then on oldest-first sums.
Exact matches clear without the bookkeeper.
Unmatched lines are listed with the rule that failed.
The bookkeeper codes a partial payment, a lump sum or a difference, or writes the note.
Customer short-pays go to the credit and collections officer. Supplier differences stay for the next payment run.
in_practice.human_gate: Anything the rules did not clear, and any tolerance match above the controller's amount. An unknown IBAN is not cleared on amount.
data_needed: Match rules and the tolerance limit
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS match log and a short note on the open item, with the allocation chosen and the person who cleared it.

evidence.claim: AFAS auto-matches bank statements on payment reference, IBAN and invoice number, then allocates sums oldest-first. Amounts must be exact unless a tolerance is set, and lines it cannot match go to a person.
Since October 2025, Dutch banks check the payee name against the IBAN. A payer who confirms after a warning is not blocked by the bank.
Cheques are rare in this Dutch logistics setting, so the reconciliation is bank transfers and open items, not cheque deposits.

risks: Oldest-first clearing applies a lump sum to the wrong invoices when the customer paid a specific bill.
A tolerance writes off small differences that are a recurring surcharge the business should see.
Clearing on amount alone can hide a payment from a new IBAN. The bank's name check happens later, at payment, and does not protect cash already received.
research_questions: What share of CAMT lines does AFAS clear on the first rule pass today, and what tolerance is set? If the share is already very high, the remaining gain is only the tail.
What are the main causes of the misses: missing reference, one payment for many invoices, a partial payment, timing, or an unknown IBAN?
How many days after the money arrives does the credit and collections officer see a short-pay?
Do customers send remittance advices as data, or only as email text? Email-only advices keep the allocation with the person.

tasks.short: Collect payroll inputs and post the payroll journal.

today.trigger: The payroll period closes, a site sends hours, or the payroll journal is ready for finance.
steps: Collect hours and allowances from the three sites, including the shifts already worked.
Check the totals against the roster and pass exceptions to the payroll specialist.
Keep agency-worker hours out of the employee payroll and on the agency invoice.
Post the payroll journal from AFAS payroll into the ledger, or retype it.
Tie the journal to the payment file and the wage-control totals before the run is paid.
drudgery: Retyping hours from a roster into a second sheet.
Chasing the same missing cost center every period.
Re-adding a journal the payroll module already totalled.
today.time_sinks: Night-shift hours that arrive after the cut-off, the two CAOs on one roster, sickness percentages from the absence file, and agency hours mixed into the employee file.

lenses.faster: Re-keying the payroll journal and re-adding its control totals disappear when the payroll module posts the journal. Chasing missing hours from the sites, and the specialist's review before payment, stay and are most of the remaining time, about three-fifths of today.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the rosters and the AFAS absence records for the period are closed. The payroll module calculates from those inputs and prepares the journal. The gate is the payroll specialist's approval of the run before anyone is paid, and the bookkeeper's hold when a site's hours do not tie.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift teams at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a morning-after window to correct an allowance before the payroll run, a group that now waits until next month's back pay. Demand would grow if the window were easy to use, because small errors are left when the correction is heavy. The payroll specialist still approves the pay.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping hours from a roster into a sheet. The work they want more of is the odd case: long sickness, a final settlement, or hours that do not match the contract.
lenses.options: A shift allowance calculated on the road-transport CAO or the warehouse CAO, and on the roster or the clock times, changes the net pay. The bookkeeper prepares the drafts. The payroll specialist chooses.
lenses.altitude: The week has fewer hours to type and more exceptions to clear before the run. The bookkeeper can hold a site whose hours do not tie to the roster, and cannot change a person's wage. The job becomes more expert on the tie-out and stays out of pay policy.
reach: The payroll specialist's assembly of the payroll journal and the control totals for finance, after the bookkeeper learns the bridge accounts and which figures they must leave untouched. CAO grading and the wage-tax return stay with the specialist.

tasks.human_edge: The person stops pay that depends on the sickness file, a final settlement or an attachment of earnings, and stops any hour line that belongs to an agency worker. Flex workers are employed by the agencies. They must not enter Noordhaven's payroll run.
tasks.pattern_why: Gross-to-net, tax tables and CAO scales are rules in the payroll engine. A model must not invent a wage. The bookkeeper's part is the hours tie-out and the journal, both checks with a fixed approval before payment.

in_practice.trigger: Site hours and AFAS absence records are closed for the payroll period.
steps: Hours that tie to the roster flow into the payroll module. A site that does not tie is held.
The module calculates pay from the employee record, the applicable CAO and the absence percentage.
Agency hours stay on the agency-invoice check and never enter this run.
The payroll journal is posted to the ledger from the module, and the bookkeeper ties it to the payment total.
The payroll specialist approves the run. Only then is the payment file released.
in_practice.human_gate: The payroll specialist approves every run before payment. The bookkeeper holds a cost center whose hours do not tie, and escalates sickness, final pay and attachments. No individual wage is changed by the bookkeeper or by a model.
data_needed: Rosters and clock times by site and shift
Employee record with the applicable CAO
Absence records that drive sick pay
Payroll bridge accounts and control totals
A marker that keeps agency workers out of the employee run
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payroll and the journal audit: who released the hours, who approved the run, and which cost center was held. Individual pay lines stay visible only to the roles that may see them.

evidence.claim: Flex workers' wage tax and VAT sit with the staffing agency. Noordhaven manages hirer's liability with records, a payment-behaviour statement and the g-rekening, which only works if those workers are not run through its own payroll by mistake.
Wage calculation from hours, tax tables and CAO scales is a rules engine. A generative model should not set pay, and the digest keeps payroll input on deterministic checks with a person approving.

risks: The two CAOs are easy to mix on one roster, and an agency worker posted as an employee is a legal error, not a coding error.
Sick pay that ignores the absence file can breach the Wet verbetering poortwachter record and the CAO rate.
A new way of processing pay data can need works-council consent and a stated AVG purpose. Individual wages must not be sent to a general model.
A tool that proposes or changes pay can fall under the employment rules of the EU AI Act. The calculation stays in the payroll engine, with the specialist approving the run.
research_questions: Which payroll actions does this role perform today: hour collection, the journal, the payment file, or employee questions? If the answer is almost none, this task should stay with the payroll specialist.
Where do warehouse hours originate, and what share from the night shift arrives after the cut-off?
How is the employee record marked for the road-transport CAO versus the warehouse CAO, and how are agency workers excluded from the run?
Has the works council agreed the current payroll processing, and who may see an individual pay line? A change that needs consent and does not have it should stop.

tasks.short: Calculate and send customer invoices and account statements.

today.trigger: A customer period is ready to bill, or a customer asks for a statement of the account.
steps: Collect billable quantities from the sites, often from a spreadsheet.
Apply the contract rate, or type a price when the rate is missing.
Calculate VAT and the total and raise the invoice in AFAS.
Send the invoice, usually as a PDF, and file a copy.
Prepare an account statement from the open items when the customer, or the credit officer, asks.
drudgery: Copying quantities from a site sheet onto the invoice.
Retyping a rate that is already in the contract.
Building a statement that the open items already contain.
today.time_sinks: Waiting hours and site surcharges the rate card does not name, credit notes, customers with their own invoice layout, and quantities that arrive late from a site.

lenses.faster: Building a standard invoice from a stored rate and a recorded quantity disappears, and statements come from the open items. A charge the rate card does not name, and every credit note, still take several minutes each, so about two-fifths of today's time remains.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the period's quantities are recorded and the customer has a rate card. AFAS calculates VAT and the total, and prepares the statement from open items. The gate is a missing rate, a first invoice for a new customer, and any credit note.
lenses.ambitious: A new weekly list for the two FP&A analysts shows handled work at each site that is not yet on an invoice, so the forecast includes revenue the team has not typed. Demand would grow in busy weeks, when volume runs ahead of billing and a cheap list would be used every week.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying quantities from a site sheet onto an invoice. The work they want more of is a rate the contract does not cover, and the credit note that follows a real dispute.
lenses.options: Billing the contract rate or the spot rate, with the fuel surcharge included or left off, changes what the customer owes and what revenue the forecast shows. The draft that is sent is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week is exception invoices, credit notes and the unbilled list, and the bookkeeper can release invoices that match the rate card and hold one that does not. The job becomes more expert on tariffs and on credit notes.
reach: The credit and collections officer's standard account statement and first reminder, after the bookkeeper learns the dunning steps and which customers are already in dispute. The officer keeps the call and any payment arrangement.

tasks.human_edge: The person prices a charge the rate card does not name, such as waiting time or a one-off site surcharge, and releases a credit note large enough to move the customer's balance. Standard lines can follow the card. These cannot.
tasks.pattern_why: Quantity times the stored rate, plus the VAT treatment, is a calculation with a written procedure. AFAS can raise that invoice and the statement from open items. Non-standard charges and credit notes stay with the person because the price is a commercial decision.

in_practice.trigger: Billable quantities for the period are in, and the customer has a rate card on SharePoint or in AFAS.
steps: Standard storage, handling and transport lines are priced from the rate card and the quantities.
AFAS calculates VAT and the invoice total.
Lines with no rate, and all credit notes, wait for the bookkeeper.
Invoices that match the card are released as a batch. Statements are produced from open items.
Work that was handled and not billed is listed per site for FP&A.
in_practice.human_gate: A missing or ambiguous rate, the first invoice for a new customer, and every credit note. Credit notes above the controller's limit need the controller as well.
data_needed: Billable quantities by site and customer
The controller's limit on credit notes
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS sales invoicing: rate card version, quantity source, who released the batch, and who released each credit note.

evidence.claim: The cabinet has chosen mandatory B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031. That choice is not law yet.
On a Peppol provider's reading of the Dutch plans, a PDF is not an e-invoice.
Billing from agreed rates and recorded quantities is a rules calculation. The digest assigns billing and account statements to deterministic software, with a person on the exceptions.

risks: A wrong rate card bills every shipment for that customer until someone complains.
Credit notes released by one person can move revenue without the controller seeing it.
A PDF invoice will not qualify as an e-invoice if the planned B2B mandate starts on 1 July 2030.
Adding statutory interest by default can breach the customer contract and damage a shipper relationship.
research_questions: Where do billable quantities live, and what share of an invoice is typed from a site spreadsheet? If quantities are not recorded anywhere structured, the invoice cannot be calculated.
What share of invoice lines uses a stored rate, and what share uses a price typed on the invoice?
How many credit notes are issued in a month, who may release one, and is every standard invoice also released by a person today?
Which customers already require UBL or Peppol? If almost none do, the current gain is the rate card, while the 2030 date still governs the format.

tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and employee expense reports.

today.trigger: A buyer or a site asks for a purchase order, or an employee hands in receipts.
steps: Read the request in Outlook or the receipt photo.
Type the order: supplier, amount, site and ledger account. Or type the receipt: merchant, amount and VAT.
Check the expense against the policy on SharePoint.
Send the order, or submit the expense claim in AFAS for approval.
Chase a missing receipt or a missing approver.
drudgery: Typing amounts and VAT off receipt photos and thermal paper.
Retyping an order the requester already described in mail.
Sending back claims for a missing cost center.
today.time_sinks: Receipts with mixed or unreadable VAT, approvers who are on shift, and night-shift repairs that were bought first and invoiced afterwards with no order.

lenses.faster: Typing receipt fields, and typing routine order lines for a known supplier and price, disappear. Each expense claim still needs a minute or two against the policy, and an emergency order still needs a morning decision, so a bit more than half of today's time remains.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when an employee submits a receipt or a night shift submits an emergency request. A model reads the receipt into amount, VAT and merchant, and a known supplier can fill a draft order. The bookkeeper approves each claim and each emergency order before it is sent.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift team leads, who now buy a small urgent repair and send the invoice afterwards, get an emergency purchase request that waits for the bookkeeper's release in the morning. Demand would grow if that path were lighter than today's, because the spend already happens and simply bypasses the order.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing amounts off receipt photos. The work they want more of is a claim that may not be business, and an urgent buy that should have been an order.
lenses.options: Raising an emergency order to the usual contractor, charging the site maintenance budget, or holding it for a buyer changes whether the night shift can finish the repair and which budget is hit. The draft changes that operational decision.
lenses.altitude: Mornings are policy exceptions and emergency orders, with less receipt typing. The bookkeeper can release an expense that matches the policy and an order under a set limit for a known supplier, and can stop one that does not. The buyer keeps supplier choice above that limit. The job becomes more expert on policy and on urgent spend.
reach: The accountant's check of VAT deductibility on employee receipts, after the bookkeeper learns the blocked cases, including representation and mixed private use, and the expense policy on SharePoint. The accountant keeps the VAT return.

tasks.human_edge: The person decides whether a receipt is business use under the expense policy, and whether a night-shift purchase was actually urgent. The model can read the amount. It should not decide that a dinner was representation or that a repair could have waited.
tasks.pattern_why: A routine order for a known supplier and a known price is a template and needs no model. A receipt photo is messy input, and one model call turns it into amount, VAT and merchant for a person to accept. The approval steps are known in advance, so this is a fixed workflow.

in_practice.trigger: An employee submits a receipt, or a night-shift lead submits an emergency purchase request.
steps: One model call reads the receipt into merchant, amount and VAT, and shows the image beside the proposal.
The bookkeeper checks the line against the expense policy and accepts or edits it.
A routine order for a known supplier and price is filled from the template.
An emergency request becomes a draft order and waits for morning release under the limit.
Claims and orders that fail the policy or the limit go back to the employee or to the buyer.
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves every expense claim and every emergency order before it counts. Above the limit, the buyer approves the supplier. A policy exception is refused or escalated, not auto-approved.
data_needed: VAT deductibility rules for employee costs
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS: the receipt image, the proposed amount, the accepted amount, who approved, and whether the line was an emergency order.

evidence.claim: AFAS scan-and-recognise turns a PDF into an e-invoice and leaves the gaps for a person. That is the document-capture function already in the stack. It is documented for incoming invoices, not for employee receipt photos.
A proposal that still needs a person to check accounts, VAT and exceptions is digitising, and measured touchless rates disappoint when the exceptions remain.
Turning a receipt photo into a proposed expense line is one model call inside a fixed approval step. The digest assigns receipts to that pattern, with a person approving each one.

risks: An easy emergency order becomes the normal way to buy and cuts the buyer out of supplier choice.
A misread amount on a thermal receipt is approved because the claim looks small.
Receipt images can show where an employee was. They should stay in AFAS under the existing retention, and not be copied into a general mailbox or a model log.
The expense policy may already have been shared with the works council. Changing the approval path without telling them creates a dispute even when the rules themselves are unchanged.
research_questions: How many purchase orders does the bookkeeper type in a month, compared with the buyers, and how many invoices arrive with no order?
How many employee expense claims arrive per month, in what form, and how often do they breach the policy?
How often does a night shift buy first and send the invoice afterwards, at which site, and for what typical amount?
If emergency purchases are rare and expense claims are few, the hours do not justify a new tool. What is the monthly count and the error rate?

role.altitude: The week moves up from keying to the quality of supplier masters, match tolerances, rate cards and the exception queues that feed the close. The bookkeeper can set a tolerance, block a bad supplier record, release a clean billing batch and hold a file or a payroll cost center, inside limits the controller sets. The job becomes more expert.
reach: The accountant's recurring accruals, the subledger tie-out at the start of the close, and the first pass on VAT-code errors, after learning the close calendar, materiality and the transport VAT treatments.
The credit and collections officer's open-item list, account statements and first reminder, after learning which customers are in dispute and how dunning works. The officer keeps the call.
The payroll specialist's payroll-journal tie-out only, after learning the bridge accounts. Wage setting, the two CAOs and the wage-tax return stay with payroll.
role.ceiling_note: Three people at a loaded €45 an hour, each of these tasks only about 40 to 60 hours a year, so typing speed is not the limit. The limit is exception volume in close week and in the flex peak, plus gates that stay with a person: payment approval, the VAT return, the g-rekening, the 30-day rule for small suppliers, and the payroll specialist's sign-off on wages. Hours, receipts and rates that never enter AFAS cannot be fixed from the finance desk. The works council and AVG limit how far pay and expense data can be opened.
skills_to_grow: VAT treatment of transport and warehousing: domestic, intra-EU and reverse charge
Hirer's liability, the payment-behaviour statement and the g-rekening split
AFAS match rules, tolerances, supplier masters and file mappings
Reading Rabobank statements and customer remittances
Rate cards, credit-note limits and the close calendar
The expense policy and which receipt VAT is blocked
Writing a short-pay note the credit officer can act on the same day
role.ambitious_version: The three bookkeepers keep procure-to-pay and order-to-cash intact while the month is still open: agency settlements and the g-rekening, unbilled work at the three sites, and short-pays the credit officer can chase the same day. The controller's close has fewer audit adjustments, and the FP&A forecast is built on a ledger that already says what happened. Wage policy and the forecast sign-off stay where they are.
